newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot gas prices lose more ground on weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot gas prices lose more ground on weather.

text.p: U.S. spot natural gas prices, pressured by forecasts for milder weather later this week, continued to lose ground Thursday, but activiy remained light due to the Christmas and New Year's Day holidays.
With eastern stocks in fairly good shape and the 6-10 day forecast calling for mostly above-normal U.S. temperatures, most expect physical prices to stay on the defensive near-term.
"After today and tomorrow, it gets warmer. There's not much to hold it up," said one Texas producer.
December Gulf Coast prices skidded more than 30 cents from Tuesday to about the $3.50/mmBtu level.
January gas at the Gulf Coast notionally was quoted about 20 cents over December at about $3.70, off 20-30 cents from Tuesday.
December gas at the New York city-gate lost another 20-25 cents to the $3.85-3.95 range.
Midcontinent prices slipped but extremely cold weather in the region tempered the selling. Most pipes were down about a nickel to the high $3.50s.
In west Texas, Permian gas notionally fell a quarter to the $3.30s.

A Reuter poll of industry players showed most expected a weekly stock draw of between 110 and 120 bcf when the AGA report was released later today. Last year at this time, overall stocks fell by 133 bcf.
